title: Analytics tiered retention + safe snapshotting for console usage
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem:
Console usage analytics contains a mix of persona fields, free-form command inputs, and sampled payloads. Current retention is a blunt 90-day TTL which makes long-term debugging and cost analyses difficult while exposing unnecessary PII surface area. We need a deployable, auditable approach that both reduces retained PII and preserves essential debugging/slo data for longer windows without manual backfills.

Goals:
- Implement a tiered retention model: short-lived raw events (7–30d), medium-lived scrubbed snapshots (90–180d), and long-lived aggregated metrics (>=1y).
- Introduce safe snapshotting: create scrubbed, indexed snapshots of events suitable for debugging (with context but no direct identifiers) and an auditable purge marker for deletion requests.
- Provide deterministic, reversible pseudonymization where required for support investigations, with key-rotation and access controls.
- Expose tooling in Console for legal/compliance operations to request expedited erasure and to view purged manifests.

Scope (in-scope):
- ETL changes in analytics ingestion pipeline to produce snapshot tiers and scrubbed payloads.
- KV-storage and index changes to keep snapshot metadata separate from raw blobs.
- Deletion orchestration that can target both raw and snapshot tiers, with attestation logs.
- RBAC changes for console tooling to allow audited un-scrub operations for authorized roles.

Out of scope (this ticket):
- UI polishing for the Console compliance page (covered in PM design ticket).
- On-prem private deployment packaging (follow-up after API-level design stabilized).

Design approach:
1) Ingestion enrich step produces two parallel outputs: raw-event-store (short TTL) and snapshot-queue. Snapshotter consumes queue and applies privacy policy (field-level regex masking, tokenization for emails/phones, deterministic pseudonyms for user IDs) to emit snapshot records into snapshot-store with separate metadata index.
2) Snapshot retention tiers are governed by a policy engine: tier assignment is based on event type, customer opt-in flags, and detected PII severity. Policies are stored in Console as JSON blobs and versioned.
3) Deletion and purge flow: a Delete Request API writes a deletion manifest referencing keys in both stores. A coordinator saga deletes raw records first, then snapshot records; each step emits signed attestations stored in audit-log-store. A final reconciliation job validates no orphaned indices remain.
4) Emergency support mode: authorized users can create a time-bound escrow token to resolve a pseudonym to a reversible identifier; all actions are logged and require a 2nd approver.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Tiered retention policies are configurable via API and configurable per-customer.
- Snapshotter produces scrubbed snapshots with automated PII rubric applied in >=95% of sampled events (measured by unit test harness).
- Deletion manifest flow completes end-to-end in staging with attestations in audit-log-store and no orphaned indices.
- End-to-end performance impact on ingestion <10% latency increase at p95.
- Security review signed off and RBAC enforced for reversible-pseudonym actions.

Implementation steps:
- Create snapshot-queue and snapshot-store schemas and migrations.
- Implement privacy policy engine library with field rule DSL and unit tests.
- Build snapshotter worker with batching and idempotency keys.
- Add deletion-manifest coordinator and attestation writer.
- Add Console API endpoints for policy management and purge requests.
- Add monitoring (metrics + traces) and SLO dashboard.

Monitoring and rollout:
- Canary rollout for 10% of traffic with snapshotting enabled; compare cost and count delta vs control.
- Dashboards: snapshot-generation-rate, scrub-failure-rate, deletion-manifest-latency, attestation-write-errors.
- Alert thresholds: scrub-failure-rate >0.5% for 15m, deletion-manifest-latency >10m for >5% of manifests.
- Runbook for failed reconciliation includes steps to trigger manual audit and re-run reconciler.

Risks and mitigations:
- Over-scrubbing reduces debug value: mitigate by having per-project opt-in fields for higher-fidelity snapshots and sampling of reversible-pseudo keys under strict audit.
- Reversible pseudonym misuse: mitigate via mandatory 2-approver flow, short TTL escrow tokens, and KMS-backed key rotation policies.
- Performance regressions at high QPS: mitigate with incremental rollout and autoscaling snapshotter worker pools; prioritize async processing.

Notes and references:
- Builds on prior privacy infra work (ENG-4729 event-level deletion pipeline) but focuses on preserving debugability via snapshots rather than full erasure only.
- Privacy rubric draft: confluence.redwood/Console/Privacy-Rubric (design doc placeholder).

Snapshotter achieves >=95% PII detection on unit/sample harness
Deletion manifest end-to-end test passes in staging with attestations
Ingestion p95 latency regression <10% in canary
Security review completed and reversible-pseudonym RBAC enforced

Deletion coordinator saga and attestation writer
Console API endpoints for policy/purge management
monitoring_and_rollout: Canary 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 3 weeks with dashboards for scrub-rate and deletion latencies. Critical alerting for scrub failures and manifests taking >10m.

Pseudonym misuse: require 2-approver escrow + short TTL tokens
Throughput impact: autoscale snapshotter and async processing
